bounded_findings: Cases0,5: actual idle declaration deletion calls original custom deleteProc even while held method-name cache headers survive; releasing cached selector headers while declaration survives does not itself call the method deleteProc.

Case1: self-deletion of a named active custom method leaves deleteProc unreached inside the original call; it reaches once after that call returns. The entered chain retains original Method records, while idle cached chains do not.

Case2: the derived override deletes the inherited original method before next; original inherited custom method still runs from the already entered chain and its deleteProc reaches after the active chain completes. This supports retaining all originally entered records, not only the current step.

Case3: same-name idle public replacement immediately reaches old deleteProc; later invocation of the original selector calls the new clientData. Observed token address equality is diagnostic and does not establish a generation receipt.

Case4: same-record public replacement DURING original custom call immediately reaches old deleteProc before that call ends; nested dispatch reaches the new clientData. Method record lifetime and mutable clientData/payload lifetime are distinct. No blanket old-payload retention rule follows from active record AddRef.
Cases6,7: declaring-class and interpreter teardown reach original deleteProc even while cache headers survive. Subsequent cache release does not repeat method deletion.

All custom token String callbacks remain unreached in raw supported rows; method-data release takes token refs from2 to1, preserving the independent caller hold. Explicit RESULT presentation is a separate channel.
C86 uses original MethodType v1/int API; C90/C91 use actual MethodType2/Tcl_Size APIs. C84/C85/Jim lanes establish only actual initialized availability for this fixed core SDK.
source_owner_conclusion: Cached chains should observe exact original Method records weakly. A validated actual entry upgrades and retains every original chain record through entered completion/next. Same-record replacement mutates and retires clientData immediately; current method-kind execution roles remain independent and must not be inferred from the custom MethodType record proof.
limits: Finite eight cases only, with held original headers/clientData objects as authored. No general optional-package absence, Native generation/address identity, receiver/frame creation permission, or Rust implementation/test pass.
BodyCallable, Forward and Property clientData per-call ownership requires their own original source/API contract; custom MethodType does not certify blanket Method payload cloning.
